intro.headline: Hands-on design leadership for products people have to trust.
intro.sub: I build teams and AI-native design systems that keep quality high.

portfolio.title: Selected work
portfolio.lede: Case studies from Strava, SRAM and SuppCo, each with my role and what changed.

leadership.title: How I lead
leadership.lede: I build the team and the operating system around it: research, rituals, career growth and design systems.

principles.title: Stay in the work
principles.body: I design alongside the team, so my feedback comes from the work, not from a distance.

principles.title: Enable others
principles.body: Research, critique and design systems that help everyone make good calls without me in the room.

principles.title: Unblock the team
principles.body: Design should be a lubricant, not a tollbooth. I keep a fast, informal SLA on questions and reviews, with feedback in open threads.

principles.title: Judgment is the job
principles.body: Making the hard calls early. Integrity Compass, which I co-created, is one example: it brings privacy, safety and inclusion into the room before launch.

stats.label: Designers on Strava’s team, grown in two years
Product designers I led at SRAM
People across product and engineering using the research practice I set up

points: Grew the design team from 5 to 15 in two years, managing five direct and about ten indirect reports across Trust & Safety, Growth, Web Platform and Foundations.
Promoted designers into staff and management roles.
Co-created Integrity Compass, a pre-launch inclusion, privacy and safety review. One session ran nine product teams through it.
Led six product designers across the AXS rider app, web, and factory and dealer tools, and hired three in my first six months.
Stood up a research practice: field A/B testing at Sea Otter and a Dovetail repository adopted by 73 people across product and engineering.
Defined the AXS app’s mission and primary KPI (“Ready to Ride”) with senior leadership.
Led product design as a player-coach, managing one product designer and reporting to the CEO.
Made the design system AI-native, so designers, engineers, and agents build from one source of truth.

work.title: Designing for Trust
work.summary: Redesigned Strava’s privacy controls so athletes could understand, and choose, exactly what they share.
work.outcome: Within a month, more than a quarter of active athletes reviewed the new controls, and 27% of them changed a setting.

image.alt: Strava privacy controls: the privacy settings list, profile page visibility, and the Heatmap opt-out

work.title: Agentic Design System
work.summary: Made SuppCo’s design system AI-native, so designers, engineers and agents build from one source of truth.
work.outcome: I raised Figma-to-code token parity from 50% to 97% in eight weeks, and packaged the system as agent skills in the repo.

image.alt: Capsule design system: agent skills repo, product sticker sheet, and TESTED catalog screen

work.title: Surfacing Value
work.summary: A strategic redesign of Strava’s information architecture and navigation, for clarity, scale and growth.
work.outcome: I facilitated the sprint. 84% of subscribers rated the new navigation better; the test modeled +$3.3M a year in net bookings.

work.title: Crushing the Basics
work.summary: Re-oriented the team around the AXS app’s core value: battery status, firmware updates and connectivity.
work.outcome: I built it on a 10,000-rider survey and 25 stakeholder interviews. It became the product group’s plan for the year.

work.title: StackScore
work.summary: Redesigned SuppCo’s signature score into a hub that explains itself and tells members what to do next.
work.role: Designer (product and engineering owned the scoring logic)
work.outcome: I designed a score-update prompt; in an A/B test, it raised score updates 24% for both free and Pro members.

image.alt: SuppCo StackScore app screens: the score overview ring, Quality tab, and Goals tab

work.title: Buying Club
work.summary: Designed SuppCo’s first commerce product, a members’ club that sells trusted supplements without discounts.
work.role: Responsible for design, alongside the Head of Product
work.outcome: In alpha, 56% of carts became orders, 41% of purchases were subscriptions, and 54% of buyers reordered within 45 days.

image.alt: SuppCo Buying Club app screens: onboarding, product page with member credits, and the Buying Club hub

about.title: Hi, I’m Andy.

photo.alt: Andy Detskas walking up the steps of a sunlit, whitewashed courtyard

about.body: I lead design for products people have to trust: privacy and safety at Strava, connected bikes at SRAM, and supplement trust at SuppCo (acquired by Function Health). I’m a player-coach who does the work alongside my team and builds the systems around it.
about.more: For inspiration, I love to watch movies, travel and shoot photos, and spend time learning about the craftsmanship that goes into building watches and bikes. I love creative endeavors that blend the technical and creative.
